claim_decisions.source_and_locator: Good 1958 publisher summary, paragraphs 1–2; Cooley et al. 1967 pp. 1675–1676
claim_decisions.rationale: Factorial interactions and analogous Fourier shortcuts are explicit. Technology/software and capability are catalogue classifications, not historical priority; publisher summary inspected via search service, not a claim of full-text inspection.

claim_decisions.source_and_locator: Good 1958 publisher metadata and summary; Cooley et al. 1967 p. 1676
claim_decisions.rationale: Publisher attributes paper to I. J. Good and first publication July 1958; his contribution is authorship. This is a publication date and first retained event, not invention date or global priority. Concept groups fast discrete Fourier methods; Cooley et al. describe Good’s distinct prime-factor algorithm.
Bibliography cites 1960 addendum, but the repair did not inspect its original text or verify month or contents; defer event.

claim_decisions.source_and_locator: Golay 1949 p. 657, columns 1 and 3 and table I
claim_decisions.rationale: Golay describes block error-correcting binary and ternary schemes, under stated bounded-error assumptions. Technology/software and capability are classification.

claim_decisions.source_and_locator: Golay 1949 p. 657 footnote, signed author line, reprint footer
claim_decisions.rationale: Note received 23 February 1949; footer identifies June 1949 Proceedings publication; author is Marcel J. E. Golay. Receipt precedes publication and is not public circulation or priority.

claim_decisions.source_and_locator: Ludwig and Taylor, Voyager Telecommunications §§3.6.2.2–3.6.3; NTRS 1979 article abstract
claim_decisions.rationale: Chapter reports Golay algorithm used at Jupiter and Saturn and separately dates Jupiter encounter 1979. NTRS describes completed Voyager 1 Jupiter encounter, but its publication date alone is not the encounter date. No claim of all telemetry.

Golay credits Shannon’s seven-symbol example and explicitly extends its solution; candidate builds_on points from 1948 Shannon paper to 1949 note. Author account alone does not satisfy independent corroboration for established edge; does not imply dependence on Hamming.

claim_decisions.source_and_locator: Michels July 1966 report, title page, abstract p. v and introduction p. 1
claim_decisions.rationale: Report date is July 1966. It reports FFT implemented in IRIS reduction and simulation programs, and separately explains use of Cooley FORTRAN IV routine. Passage does not establish same specific program in IRIS or flight use. This dated report is a new event beyond 1964 receipt and 1965 publication in base.

claim_decisions.source_and_locator: Cooley and Tukey 1965 p. 297; Cooley, Lewis and Welch 1967 pp. 1675–1676
claim_decisions.rationale: 1965 authors discuss Good generalization and application; 1967 authors distinguish prime-factor and Cooley–Tukey algorithms. Candidate direction Good to 1965 is supported as author-described connection, but 1967 shares Cooley and is not independent corroboration for established relation. Replacing missing prerequisite note with a represented candidate is appropriate.

claim_decisions.source_and_locator: Good publisher author metadata; Golay 1949 p. 657 signed author line
claim_decisions.rationale: Names and sourced basis supported; no biography inferred. Merge by ID and verify no duplicate IDs, using exact canonical row hashes.
